rules.title: Read of /etc/shadow by a process that has no business reading it

tests.name: match: an unknown binary in /tmp reading /etc/gshadow
nomatch: sudo's PAM helper (the original false positive)
nomatch: useradd writing the shadow file is a write, not a read

queries.duckdb: SELECT uid, time, hostname, product, user_name, process_name, process_path, cmd_line, parent_path, target_file, dst_ip, dst_port FROM ocsf_flat WHERE time >= ? AND time < ? AND class_uid = 1001 AND activity_id = 2 AND ((coalesce(target_file ILIKE '/etc/shadow' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(target_file ILIKE '/etc/gshadow' ESCAPE '\', false)) AND NOT (coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/unix\_chkpwd' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/passwd' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/chpasswd' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/chage' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/useradd' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/usermod' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/userdel' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/groupadd' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/sshd' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/login' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/su' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/sudo' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/cron' ESCAPE '\', false))) ORDER BY time

rules.tuned_from: First version alerted on every sudo, because sudo's PAM stack runs unix_chkpwd, which reads /etc/shadow. The PAM helpers and the password tools now sit in a filter, matched by path suffix so a renamed copy elsewhere still alerts.
rules.description: Tetragon's security_file_permission hook reports every open of /etc/shadow. Password tooling and PAM helpers read it all day; anything else reading it is credential access until proven otherwise.

rules.title: Crontab replaced from a file

tests.name: match: crontab installed from a file (Atomic T1053.003 test 1)

queries.duckdb: SELECT uid, time, hostname, product, user_name, process_name, process_path, cmd_line, parent_path, target_file, dst_ip, dst_port FROM ocsf_flat WHERE time >= ? AND time < ? AND class_uid = 1007 AND activity_id = 1 AND (coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/crontab' ESCAPE '\', false) AND coalesce(regexp_matches(cmd_line, 'crontab\s+(-u\s+\S+\s+)?[^-\s]\S*\s*$'), false)) ORDER BY time

rules.description: "crontab FILE" swaps the whole crontab for the contents of a file, which is how scripted persistence installs a job. Listing (-l), editing (-e) and removing (-r) are excluded.

rules.title: Local account created with useradd or adduser

tests.name: match: useradd from the Atomic runner
nomatch: the shell that called it
nomatch: useradd exiting is not a creation

queries.duckdb: SELECT uid, time, hostname, product, user_name, process_name, process_path, cmd_line, parent_path, target_file, dst_ip, dst_port FROM ocsf_flat WHERE time >= ? AND time < ? AND class_uid = 1007 AND activity_id = 1 AND (coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/useradd' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%/adduser' ESCAPE '\', false)) ORDER BY time

rules.description: A new local account inside a container or on a server is persistence unless a change ticket says otherwise.

rules.title: LSASS memory dump through comsvcs.dll MiniDump

queries.duckdb: SELECT uid, time, hostname, product, user_name, process_name, process_path, cmd_line, parent_path, target_file, dst_ip, dst_port FROM ocsf_flat WHERE time >= ? AND time < ? AND class_uid = 1007 AND activity_id = 1 AND (coalesce(cmd_line ILIKE '%comsvcs%' ESCAPE '\', false) AND coalesce(cmd_line ILIKE '%minidump%' ESCAPE '\', false)) ORDER BY time

rules.description: rundll32 calling comsvcs.dll's MiniDump export is a living-off-the-land LSASS dump that needs no tooling on disk.

rules.title: PowerShell started with an encoded command

tests.name: match: the shortest prefix, -ec, in pwsh
nomatch: Linux pwsh in the Atomic runner pod (the emulator's own transport)

queries.duckdb: SELECT uid, time, hostname, product, user_name, process_name, process_path, cmd_line, parent_path, target_file, dst_ip, dst_port FROM ocsf_flat WHERE time >= ? AND time < ? AND class_uid = 1007 AND activity_id = 1 AND ((coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\', false)) AND coalesce(regexp_matches(cmd_line, '(?i)\s[-/](e|ec|en|enc|enco|encod|encode|encoded|encodedc|encodedco|encodedcom|encodedcomm|encodedcomma|encodedcomman|encodedcommand)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{8,}'), false)) ORDER BY time

rules.description: -EncodedCommand (and every prefix PowerShell accepts for it, down to -e and -ec) hides the script from anyone reading the command line. Legitimate tooling rarely needs it on a workstation.

rules.title: Scheduled task created to run at startup or logon

queries.duckdb: SELECT uid, time, hostname, product, user_name, process_name, process_path, cmd_line, parent_path, target_file, dst_ip, dst_port FROM ocsf_flat WHERE time >= ? AND time < ? AND class_uid = 1007 AND activity_id = 1 AND (coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) AND coalesce(cmd_line ILIKE '%/create%' ESCAPE '\', false) AND (coalesce(cmd_line ILIKE '%onstart%' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(cmd_line ILIKE '%onlogon%' ESCAPE '\', false))) ORDER BY time

rules.description: schtasks /create with an ONSTART or ONLOGON trigger is a classic way to survive a reboot.

rules.title: Windows system process name running from the wrong folder

tests.name: match: lsass.exe from C:\Windows\Temp (Atomic T1036.003 test 1)
match: svchost.exe in a user profile
nomatch: case does not matter for the folder either

queries.duckdb: SELECT uid, time, hostname, product, user_name, process_name, process_path, cmd_line, parent_path, target_file, dst_ip, dst_port FROM ocsf_flat WHERE time >= ? AND time < ? AND class_uid = 1007 AND activity_id = 1 AND ((coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\csrss.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\smss.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\wininit.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\winlogon.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\services.exe' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE '%\\lsm.exe' ESCAPE '\', false)) AND NOT (coalesce(process_path ILIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\%' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\%' ESCAPE '\', false) OR coalesce(process_path ILIKE 'C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\%' ESCAPE '\', false))) ORDER BY time

rules.description: lsass.exe, svchost.exe, csrss.exe and friends only ever run from System32 (or SysWOW64). The same name anywhere else is masquerading: a renamed tool hoping to blend into a process list.
